name: Reims

art.title: Szeptycki's Lancers Taking Prussians at Reims

summary: Napoleon fell on Saint-Priest's Russian and Prussian corps, which had taken Reims; Saint-Priest, an émigré Frenchman in Russian service, was mortally wounded, and the city was retaken.

toCome.name: Marmont's Corps
toCome.formation: Ricard's division and Pelleport's brigade, VI Corps, with Bordesoulle's I Cavalry Corps
toCome.summary: Led the march on Reims, catching Prussian cavalry at Rosnay and Jagow's Landwehr at Ormes; Ricard's division took the Sainte-Geneviève heights before the town and failed to storm the Soissons gate.

toCome.name: Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur
toCome.formation: Cavalry Division, with Piquet's and Ségur's brigades
toCome.summary: Led the assault with Ricard's division; Ségur's brigade, with the 3rd Gardes d'Honneur, was trapped and largely destroyed.

toCome.name: Sébastiani's Guard Cavalry
toCome.summary: Advanced on Ricard's flanks; Exelmans's division crossed the Vesle and led the pursuit.

toCome.name: The Guard and Ney's Infantry
toCome.formation: Friant's Old Guard and Boyer de Rébeval's divisions
toCome.summary: Came up in the afternoon and were held back; sixteen of the Guard's guns blew in the Soissons gate.

toCome.name: Saint-Priest's Corps
toCome.formation: Gurgalov's 11th and Pillar's 17th Divisions, with Emmanuel's dragoons, VIII Infantry Corps
toCome.summary: About eight thousand men, who had taken Reims the day before. Saint-Priest was mortally wounded by a shell, and the corps fell back through the town in disorder.

toCome.name: Jagow's Brigade
toCome.summary: About five thousand men, surprised and broken at Gueux, Muizon and Thillois.
